attacks.claim: The conflict rule is only defined for the case where both sides changed since last sync. Other sync edge cases (e.g., an unsynced slot whose server copy was deleted by the 24-month purge while the player was away, or a local save with a newer timestamp but a corrupted/unreadable cloud copy) are not specified, and the 'newest cloud copy' rule can silently overwrite local progress based on device clock timestamps that may be wrong.
attacks.evidence: "On launch the game downloads the newest cloud copy if the local slot is older." / ABSENT: behaviour when timestamps come from devices with skewed clocks, and when the local slot is newer but its last-sync base is unknown.

attacks.claim: The server keeps only the last 5 versions per slot and the game keeps 3 local backups; with 2-device play and frequent sync, a player who repeatedly launches on a device with a stale or wrong save can push good versions out of the 5-version window, so the 'every replaced version is kept' promise can fail in practice. Retention interaction is not analysed.
attacks.evidence: "Every replaced version is kept: the server keeps the last 5 versions per slot, and the game keeps the last 3 locally"

attacks.claim: The 'no lost save' guarantee is supported only by 11 conflict prompts and a 4-PC test plus a 30-player-day beta; the load test covers launch-time concurrency but not the upload-after-replace path, partial upload failure, or a crash mid-download. The claim that 'players must never lose a save' is not demonstrated for interrupted writes.
attacks.evidence: "0 lost saves; 11 conflict prompts, all resolved by players." / ABSENT: test of app crash or network drop during download/overwrite of the local save file.

attacks.claim: Epic under-13 handling is described only as 'linking not offered', but the data minimisation and consent path for the cabined accounts (e.g., whether any sync data for them is still uploaded automatically, and whether parental consent rules apply to the sidecar device name) is not addressed; the device name field is personal-adjacent data stored on the server.
attacks.evidence: "for them linking is not offered and the screen explains why." / "sync.meta sidecar (slot, playtime, last-modified, device name)"

attacks.claim: Device name is stored server-side and linkable to a Steam/Epic ID; the artifact says no personal data beyond IDs but device names can contain real names. Minor since it is not clearly a violation.
attacks.evidence: "We store: Steam ID, Epic account ID, save blobs, sync.meta." and sidecar includes "device name"

attacks.claim: Cost math: 420 KB × 5 versions × 10 slots × opt-in players is not reconciled with the 140 GB forecast, and egress at $90/month has no per-player ceiling; the 60 uploads/hour limit allows large egress bursts. Budget stop at $600 would flip the kill switch mid-session, a reliability issue but already mitigated.
attacks.evidence: "forecast ~140 GB at 60% opt-in, about $3/month. Requests and egress ~$90/month."

attacks.claim: The rollback to 1.3 relies on 1.3 ignoring sidecar and modifier keys, but 1.4-written saves with new modifiers could leave players in a state where modifiers are silently dropped on 1.3, and cloud copies written by 1.4 remain on the server after rollback with no documented cleanup.
attacks.evidence: "saves written by 1.4 are the same v3 format and load in 1.3 (tested above)."
